pages: From Weight of Evidence to Logistic Regression
Did you know that there is a direct way to convert Weight of Evidence (WOE) scores to logistic regression estimates for univariate categorical data?

Univariate logistic regression (one category)* *See Appendix for a complete decomposition. Dataset is from https://academic.oup.com/aje/article-abstract/179/2/252/123902. https://academic.oup.com/aje/article-abstract/179/2/252/123902
Univariate logistic regression (several categories)* * Dataset used is ResumeNames from Applied Econometrics with R (AER). Target is ‘computer’.

From univarite target encoding to logistic regression 0.87 0.81 Average rate (y) Manufacturing 0.85 Health/education/social services 0.92 1.43 1.77 2.48 -0.45 -0.11 0.61 Log odds Weight of Evidence* Business/personal services Encoded probabilities of class 1 Convert to log odds and WOE Below average Above average Δ=0.34 Δ=0.34 Δ=1.05 Δ=1.05 * WOE can be derived from two probabilities as log(0.81/(1-0.81)) – log(0.87/(1-0.87)) = -0.45 Logistic regression (MLE) coefficients: b0 (intercept) = 1.43, b1 = 0.34, b2 = 1.05 ✅
WOE is effectively another way to frame the evidence captured by logistic regression coefficients in the single feature case
